items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: He later went on to play with Count Basie’s band and Ray Charles and different people like that.

ctx.x: He was a sax player, wasn’t he?

See you’re good, yeah. That’s when I went with him. We played at Count Basie’s club because Count Basie was managing them at the time. He later went on to play with Count Basie’s band and Ray Charles and different people like that. So I came with that band in the spring. And I made a contact with different people. Made contacts you know. And then that fall a childhood friend of mine who was a trumpet player, his name was Jerry Ayers, he came to his grandmother’s funeral and so he was in town for three or four…
So then you started getting calls, maybe to sub for people? “Hey I can’t make my gig tonight, can you cover for me?” Is that how that works?
